answer: Cross-community bridge vouching: a new identity needs three established cosigners from mutually independent communities, each locking a 200 saffron-credit bond in its home ledger. Because the bridge graph is public, one sponsor cannot vouch twice across groups; the 5th fake demands 15 unrelated vouchers. Each epoch 20% of bridges are re-audited, seeded by the delta of the epoch hash, and a caught forgery burns every sponsor bond on that path. Verification is replayable: anyone recomputes the drawn bridges, so cost scales superlinearly with cluster size while honest agents pay once.
